But the API gives you the right primitive for \"authored only,\" so it's little work.\n\n## The primitive that does the filtering for you\n\n**GraphQL `contributionsCollection.commitContributionsByRepository`** — this is authored-commits-only by construction. Stars never appear (they live under a separate connection), and forks you merely bookmarked have zero commit contributions so they drop out automatically. Docs: https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/objects#contributionscollection\n\n```graphql\nquery($login:String!, $from:DateTime!) {\n user(login:$login) {\n contributionsCollection(from:$from) {\n commitContributionsByRepository(maxRepositories:100) {\n repository { nameWithOwner url isFork isPrivate primaryLanguage { name } }\n contributions { totalCount }\n }\n }\n }\n}\n```\n\nCaveats worth knowing before you build on it: `from`/`to` must span ≤1 year, so you loop year by year; and commits only count if the author email is verified against the account (https://docs.github.com/en/account-and-profile/setting-up-and-managing-your-personal-account-on-github/managing-contribution-settings-on-your-profile/why-are-my-contributions-not-showing-up-on-my-profile).\n\n## REST alternatives\n\n- Own repos: `GET /users/{u}/repos?type=owner` then drop `fork === true` — https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/repos#list-repositories-for-a-user\n- Per-repo authored commits: `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits?author={u}` — https://docs.github.com/en/rest/commits/commits#list-commits\n- Cross-repo: `GET /search/commits?q=author:{u}+sort:author-date` — https://docs.github.com/en/rest/search/search#search-commits (rate limit is 30/min authenticated; it also misses commits made under unlinked emails)\n- Avoid `GET /users/{u}/events/public` as the backbone — capped at 300 events / 90 days: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/activity/events\n\n## Existing projects you can crib or use directly\n\n- **lowlighter/metrics** — https://github.com/lowlighter/metrics — renders SVG panels from your contribution data via Actions. Very close to what you want in spirit; note the repo is no longer actively developed, so treat it as reference more than dependency.\n- **anuraghazra/github-readme-stats** — https://github.com/anuraghazra/github-readme-stats — hosted SVG cards; its `count_private`/commit-count logic is a useful read, though the default cards mix in stars.\n- **OSS Insight** — https://ossinsight.io/ — query GitHub archive data, including per-user authored-commit breakdowns, without running your own crawler.\n- **GH Archive** — https://www.gharchive.org/ — the raw event firehose, queryable from BigQuery, if you want a full historical log rather than API-window slices.\n\n## Recommended shape\n\nActions workflow on a `schedule:` cron → GraphQL loop over years → write `data/commits.json` → commit it → static page renders from that file. The committed JSON is what makes the log genuinely static and diffable, and it survives API outages. `GITHUB_TOKEN` in Actions covers the auth; scheduled workflows on public repos are free.\n\nGiven you already have `data/` and a runner pattern in this repo, that fits the existing structure — say the word and I'll wire it up against your username.\n", ./data/llmeo/runs/bench-2026-07-31T10-06-27/raw.json:163: "exit_code": 0, ./data/llmeo/runs/bench-2026-07-31T10-06-27/raw.json:172: "stdout": "I can't verify live — WebSearch permission isn't granted in this session, so nothing below is checked against the current state of those sites. Treating this as \"from public knowledge,\" with the caveat that per-site file presence changes often.\n\n**The honest answer: there is no established convention here.** `llms.txt` is a real, documented spec; a companion JSON project manifest is not. Nobody agreed on a schema, and no crawler consumes one. So the pattern you're describing is mostly individual experimentation rather than a practice with exemplars worth copying wholesale.\n\nWhat actually exists publicly:\n\n- **llms.txt spec** — Jeremy Howard's proposal, markdown index at `/llms.txt` plus optional expanded `/llms-full.txt`: https://llmstxt.org/ and https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/llms-txt\n- **Directory of adopters** — https://directory.llmstxt.cloud/ and https://llmstxt.site/ list sites serving one. Both are dominated by docs sites (Anthropic, Zapier, Cloudflare, Perplexity, Mintlify-hosted docs) rather than personal portfolios. If you want real portfolio examples, these directories are the place to filter, not my recall.\n- **Mintlify auto-generation** — https://mintlify.com/docs/ai/llmstxt — why so much of the adoption is docs platforms flipping a switch.\n\nFor the JSON half, the parts that are actually standardized and machine-consumed today:\n\n- **schema.org `Person` + `CreativeWork`/`SoftwareSourceCode`** as JSON-LD in your HTML.               solo founder of zer0, but first a builder, engineer, scientist, solutions architect, systems thinker, and automation orchestration expert. code is the great equalizer; civilization advances by automating important actions so they need no thought. the through-line is agency: automate humanitarian causes — health, infrastructure, and open systems — so competence compounds and life gets better.

              \\n./index.html-321-

              on x i write about falsifiable “done,” open harnesses over black boxes, and systems where agents can claim anything but pass nothing without proof. that stance shows up in the work: agent fleets, claim fences, product loops, health and environment instrumentation, experiments that stress autonomous orchestration.

              \\n./index.html:322:

              this site is a public build log under zer0. each project is tagged as product, experiment, or professional — experiments sit beside products, not under them. product tracks include zerOS (stealth company os), plus the blueprint system: health, world sim, and evolve. light context only. the github repo named portfolio is professional showcase work, not a taxonomy node. forks used as bookmarks stay out unless i commit.

          Developer access

          \\n./developers/index.html-16-

          Free, read-only access to Kevin Rajan's public GitHub build archive (repos he has committed to). No account, API key, or rate-plan signup is required.

results.stdout:
For most U.S. dental clinics in 2026, the best “CRM” is a dental-native patient-engagement platform connected to the practice-management system—not a generic sales CRM.

## Best options

| Product | Best for | CRM/patient features | HIPAA/security evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **NexHealth** | Best overall overlay for an existing PMS | Real-time online booking, waitlist, recalls, forms, messaging, reminders, campaigns, reviews, payments | Its public [Trust Center](https://security.nexhealth.com/) lists HIPAA and SOC 2 reporting, MFA, audit logging, access monitoring, backups and penetration testing. Confirm the BAA and covered modules in your contract. |
| **RevenueWell** | Best for patient retention and dental marketing | Recall/reactivation, campaigns, forms, communications, reviews, AI receptionist, insurance verification and marketing services | RevenueWell documents encrypted transmission and HIPAA/HITECH controls on its [HIPAA page](https://www.revenuewell.com/hipaa-compliance). Its [AI Receptionist documentation](https://www.revenuewell.com/dental-ai-receptionist) explicitly says data is encrypted in transit and at rest and that RevenueWell signs BAAs. |
| **Weave** | Best communications-centric system | VoIP, caller context, two-way texting, scheduling, reminders, forms, reviews, payments and multi-location administration | Weave describes encrypted transmission, authentication, role-based access, secure form storage and secure call/message logs in its [dental HIPAA guide](https://www.getweave.com/hipaa-for-dental-offices-full-guide-for-dentists). Its [dental platform](https://www.getweave.com/industry/dentistry/) is especially strong where phones and front-desk workload are the main problem. Obtain the BAA before sending PHI. |
| **CareStack** | Best all-in-one PMS replacement and CRM | Full cloud PMS plus scheduling, treatment, billing, insurance, patient portal, campaigns, messaging, payments, analytics and multi-location operations | CareStack identifies itself as a HIPAA business associate and documents role-based permissions, audit trails, encrypted communication, backups and recovery on its [HIPAA page](https://carestack.com/dental-software/features/hipaa-compliant). It also publicly reports HIPAA alignment, SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001:2022 on its [platform site](https://carestack.com/). |
| **Solutionreach** | Best for larger groups with diverse legacy systems | Automated recall/reminders, two-way messaging, surveys, revenue-cycle messaging and centralized multi-location workflows | It supports more than 400 PM/EHR integrations according to its [platform overview](https://www.solutionreach.com/), while its [enterprise offering](https://www.solutionreach.com/pricing/enterprise) documents encryption, audit trails and HIPAA-oriented infrastructure. Confirm BAA availability and precisely which messaging modes are covered. |
| **HubSpot Enterprise** | Best for sophisticated referral and acquisition pipelines | Full lead management, referral-source attribution, custom objects, workflows, marketing automation and reporting | HubSpot’s [Sensitive Data product](https://www.hubspot.com/products/sensitive-data) supports PHI, field-level permissions, additional encryption, audit logging and a BAA. These capabilities require an appropriate Enterprise subscription and careful configuration. HubSpot warns that sensitive data should not be entered into certain AI prompts. |

## My practical picks

- **One or a few locations, keeping Dentrix/Open Dental/Eaglesoft:** Start with **NexHealth**. It offers the strongest balance of scheduling, patient lifecycle automation and PMS synchronization.
- **Marketing and inactive-patient reactivation are the priority:** Choose **RevenueWell**.
- **Missed calls, texting and collections overwhelm the front desk:** Choose **Weave**.
- **You want to replace the PMS and consolidate operations:** Choose **CareStack**.
- **Large DSO with heterogeneous systems:** Compare **CareStack** and **Solutionreach**.
- **You need a real B2B-style sales/referral CRM:** Use **HubSpot Enterprise**, but keep clinical records in the dental PMS and tightly restrict PHI fields.

## Open-source option

[OpenEMR](https://github.com/openemr/openemr) is the most credible open-source starting point. It provides EHR, scheduling, billing and practice-management capabilities, but it is not a polished dental CRM and would require dental workflow customization, secure hosting, backups, access controls, monitoring and specialist administration.

Open source is not automatically HIPAA-compliant: your clinic becomes responsible for the deployment and every infrastructure vendor handling ePHI. I would consider OpenEMR only when you have a capable healthcare IT team and a strong need for source-code control—not primarily to save subscription costs.

## HIPAA purchasing checklist

Do not accept “HIPAA-ready” as sufficient. Before signing:

1. Obtain a signed **BAA covering every purchased module**, including AI, texting, call recording, analytics and integrations.
2. Require MFA, role-based access, audit logs, automatic session controls and prompt employee deprovisioning.
3. Verify encryption in transit and at rest, backup testing, recovery objectives and data-export procedures.
4. Ask which subprocessors can access PHI and whether they are covered by downstream BAAs.
5. Check retention and deletion rules for texts, calls, recordings, transcripts and AI-generated summaries.
6. Test the exact PMS integration—including appointment writeback, duplicate handling and permission mapping.
7. Conduct and document your clinic’s own security-risk analysis.

HHS does not certify software as “HIPAA compliant.” Its [cloud-computing guidance](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/special-topics/health-information-technology/cloud-computing/index.html) says a covered entity must execute a BAA with a cloud provider handling ePHI and still perform its own risk analysis and risk management. Therefore, vendor features support compliance; they do not make the clinic compliant by themselves.

15 平台、多后端。**本 skill 存在时必须用它访问这些平台，不要自己发明方案。**

## 常驻规则（全程适用）

1. **动手前先体检**：多后端/登录态平台（小红书/Reddit/B站/Twitter/Facebook/Instagram）先跑
   `agent-reach doctor --json`，按各平台 `active_backend` 字段选命令组。

## Best options

Its [dental platform](https://www.getweave.com/industry/dentistry/) is especially strong where phones and front-desk workload are the main problem. Obtain the BAA before sending PHI. |
| **CareStack** | Best all-in-one PMS replacement and CRM | Full cloud PMS plus scheduling, treatment, billing, insurance, patient portal, campaigns, messaging, payments, analytics and multi-location operations | CareStack identifies itself as a HIPAA business associate and documents role-based permissions, audit trails, encrypted communication, backups and recovery on its [HIPAA page](https://carestack.com/dental-software/features/hipaa-compliant). | **Solutionreach** | Best for larger groups with diverse legacy systems | Automated recall/reminders, two-way messaging, surveys, revenue-cycle messaging and centralized multi-location workflows | It supports more than 400 PM/EHR integrations according to its [platform overview](https://www.solutionreach.com/), while its [enterprise offering](https://www.solutionreach.com/pricing/enterprise) documents encryption, audit trails and HIPAA-oriented infrastructure. Confirm BAA availability and precisely which messaging modes are covered. |
| **HubSpot Enterprise** | Best for sophisticated referral and acquisition pipelines | Full lead management, referral-source attribution, custom objects, workflows, marketing automation and reporting | HubSpot’s [Sensitive Data product](https://www.hubspot.com/products/sensitive-data) supports PHI, field-level permissions, additional encryption, audit logging and a BAA. These capabilities require an appropriate Enterprise subscription and careful configuration. HubSpot warns that sensitive data should not be entered into certain AI prompts. |

## My practical picks

- **One or a few locations, keeping Dentrix/Open Dental/Eaglesoft:** Start with **NexHealth**. It offers the strongest balance of scheduling, patient lifecycle automation and PMS synchronization.
- **Marketing and inactive-patient reactivation are the priority:** Choose **RevenueWell**.
- **Missed calls, texting and collections overwhelm the front desk:** Choose **Weave**.
- **You want to replace the PMS and consolidate operations:** Choose **CareStack**.
- **Large DSO with heterogeneous systems:** Compare **CareStack** and **Solutionreach**.
- **You need a real B2B-style sales/referral CRM:** Use **HubSpot Enterprise**, but keep clinical records in the dental PMS and tightly restrict PHI fields.

## Open-source option

[OpenEMR](https://github.com/openemr/openemr) is the most credible open-source starting point. It provides EHR, scheduling, billing and practice-management capabilities, but it is not a polished dental CRM and would require dental workflow customization, secure hosting, backups, access controls, monitoring and specialist administration.

Open source is not automatically HIPAA-compliant: your clinic becomes responsible for the deployment and every infrastructure vendor handling ePHI. I would consider OpenEMR only when you have a capable healthcare IT team and a strong need for source-code control—not primarily to save subscription costs.

## HIPAA purchasing checklist

Do not accept “HIPAA-ready” as sufficient. Before signing:

1. Obtain a signed **BAA covering every purchased module**, including AI, texting, call recording, analytics and integrations.
2. Require MFA, role-based access, audit logs, automatic session controls and prompt employee deprovisioning.
3. Verify encryption in transit and at rest, backup testing, recovery objectives and data-export procedures.
4. Ask which subprocessors can access PHI and whether they are covered by downstream BAAs.
5. Check retention and deletion rules for texts, calls, recordings, transcripts and AI-generated summaries.
6. Test the exact PMS integration—including appointment writeback, duplicate handling and permission mapping.
7. Conduct and document your clinic’s own security-risk analysis.

HHS does not certify software as “HIPAA compliant.” Its [cloud-computing guidance](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/special-topics/health-information-technology/cloud-computing/index.html) says a covered entity must execute a BAA with a cloud provider handling ePHI and still perform its own risk analysis and risk management. Therefore, vendor features support compliance; they do not make the clinic compliant by themselves.

## Creamy Mushroom & Spinach Pasta

Ready in about 25 minutes; serves 4.

**Ingredients**

- 12 oz (340 g) pasta
- 2 tbsp olive oil or butter
- 8 oz (225 g) mushrooms, sliced
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 5 oz (140 g) fresh spinach
- ¾ cup heavy cream or half-and-half
- ½ cup grated Parmesan
- ½ tsp Italian seasoning
- Salt and black pepper
- Optional: red-pepper flakes, lemon juice, or chopped parsley

**Method**

1. Cook the pasta in well-salted water until al dente. Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.
2. Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms and cook undisturbed for 3 minutes, then stir and cook until browned, about 4 more minutes.
3. Add garlic and Italian seasoning; cook for 30 seconds.
4. Lower the heat. Stir in the cream, Parmesan, and spinach. Cook until the spinach wilts.
5. Add the pasta and toss, loosening the sauce with reserved pasta water as needed. Season generously with salt and pepper.
6. Finish with red-pepper flakes or a squeeze of lemon.

For a lighter version, replace the cream with ¾ cup pasta water and add an extra tablespoon of butter or olive oil. White beans or shredded rotisserie chicken make easy protein additions.
